scope_note: Light verification/polish pass. Joey and the canonical project already provide a strong Asclepias/milkvine layer. This package turns that species work into a family lesson while explicitly separating broad Apocynaceae characters from the derived Asclepiadoideae milkweed characters.

joey_coverage.audit_summary: Excellent Asclepias, Matelea/Gonolobinae and other Apocynaceae morphology, including follicles and seeds.
joey_coverage.assessment: Joey coverage is sufficient for the first family module. The main remaining gap is breadth outside the milkweed/asclepiadoid lineage.

live_project_scope.taxonomy_note: The live source pool retains Matelea biflora while the canonical project follows current Kew/POWO Chthamalia biflora, with Matelea biflora retained as a synonym/alternative treatment. Do not duplicate the taxon.
live_project_scope.breadth_note: The current local project pool contains no non-Asclepiadoid Apocynaceae anchor. Record that as a breadth/visual gap rather than inventing one.

family_lesson.broad_family_where_to_look_first: Start with sap, leaves and corolla: many Apocynaceae have latex, simple entire leaves commonly opposite or whorled, no stipules, a fused 5-lobed corolla, five stamens attached to the corolla tube, and a superior ovary of two carpels associated with a common style head.
family_lesson.local_milkweed_where_to_look_first: For our Asclepias and milkvine anchors, go straight to the corona + gynostegium + pollinia/pollinarium. Then confirm paired follicles or the single surviving follicle and comose seeds.
family_lesson.broad_family_correction: Gynostegium, corona, waxy pollinia/pollinaria and paired follicles characterize the more derived milkweed-side of Apocynaceae and are especially useful for the project's local Asclepiadoideae. They are not mandatory across broad Apocynaceae.
authoritative_framework: Habit ranges from herbs and climbers to shrubs and trees.
Leaves are commonly opposite or whorled, simple and entire; stipules are usually absent.
Flowers commonly have a fused tubular 5-lobed corolla and five stamens inserted on the corolla tube.
The ovary is usually superior and built from two carpels that may be free below but coordinated by the style/stylar head.
Fruit is often one or two follicles but may instead be a capsule, berry or drupe.
In derived asclepiadoid lineages the stamens and expanded stylar head form a gynostegium; pollen is packaged into pollinia/pollinaria and a corona is often present.
avoid_overgeneralizing: Do not define all Apocynaceae by a milkweed corona.
Do not require pollinia/pollinaria across the broad family.
Do not require paired follicles; one follicle may abort and other Apocynaceae lineages can make berries, drupes or capsules.
Do not use latex alone as a family ID.
Do not keep Matelea biflora and Chthamalia biflora as separate learner species.

Convolvulaceae.tie_breaker: Both may be twining and have a fused corolla. Local milkvines resolve with the gynostegium/corona/pollinarium machinery and follicle fruit; morning-glories lack that milkweed reproductive apparatus and commonly have alternate leaves and a capsule.

Gentianaceae.tie_breaker: Opposite simple leaves and fused flowers can overlap. The milkweed-side of Apocynaceae resolves with latex plus gynostegium/pollinia and follicle fruit; broad-family cases should be confirmed from floral/stylar architecture rather than leaf arrangement alone.

fast_key: Milky or clear latex + opposite/whorled entire leaves + fused 5-lobed corolla -> consider Apocynaceae.
Corona + gynostegium + pollinia/pollinarium -> derived milkweed-side of Apocynaceae.
Two carpels producing paired follicles, often with one aborting -> common milkweed fruit architecture.
Silky comose seeds released from a follicle -> strong milkweed-side cue.
Twining vine with a fused flower but no milkweed reproductive machinery -> reconsider Convolvulaceae.
Remember that broad Apocynaceae can have non-follicle fruits and lack the obvious milkweed apparatus.
